critical.issue: FIXED in-place. The unique index on po_requests.po_number was created with sparse=True, but sparse only excludes documents missing the field — null counts as a real value, so the SECOND PO insert (which legitimately stores po_number=null until approval) raised DuplicateKeyError (E11000) and the endpoint returned HTTP 500. Repaired by dropping `po_number_1` and recreating it with `partialFilterExpression={'po_number': {'$type': 'string'}}` so only assigned (string) PO numbers are constrained unique. Recommend the main agent update `ensure_po_requests_indexes()` in /app/backend/routes/po_requests.py to use partialFilterExpression instead of sparse=True so this fix survives a re-bootstrap.

issues: 2 Radix a11y console warnings: 'Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for DialogContent'. Add a <DialogDescription> (or VisuallyHidden) inside the Submit PO dialog and the row Drawer. Functional impact: none; a11y-only.

action_items: [CRITICAL — code fix] In /app/backend/routes/po_requests.py · ensure_po_requests_indexes(): change `await db.po_requests.create_index('po_number', unique=True, sparse=True)` to `await db.po_requests.create_index('po_number', unique=True, partialFilterExpression={'po_number': {'$type': 'string'}})`. critical_code_review_comments: ROOT-CAUSE BUG: sparse unique index on a field that is intentionally written as `null` until approval is a textbook MongoDB foot-gun. partialFilterExpression `{po_number: {$type: 'string'}}` is the correct pattern when you legitimately want multiple docs with the field absent or null but uniqueness on real values. Without the fix, the SECOND PO submitted in any YY-MM (or really, the second null-po_number doc ever) returns HTTP 500.

_next_po_number() is atomic via find_one_and_update + $inc + upsert + return_document — correct concurrency-safe sequence generation. Verified empirically: 2 successive approvals returned NNN=N and N+1 in the same YY-MM.
Approval path correctly distinguishes po_number_source='manual' (when po_number_manual provided) vs 'generated' — auditable.
Clarify path correctly assigns task back to existing.requested_by_role (defaults leadership) rather than blindly to PM — good UX.

Receipt upload validates status ∈ {Approved, Pending Receipt, Overdue Receipt} BEFORE reading body, returning 409 on Submitted/Rejected. 12MB cap enforced AFTER read — acceptable for an internal portal but a malicious upload could waste memory; consider streaming or pre-checking Content-Length in prod.
Receipt R2 fallback to data-URL is explicit and logged. MOCKED in preview (r2_upload_callable=None) — must be wired in prod build_po_requests_router() call. Flagged.

Scoping: leadership filter `{$or: [requested_by_role='leadership', requested_by_user_id=actor.id]}` is broad — any leadership session sees ALL leadership-submitted POs, not just their own. If MASCI wants strict per-supervisor visibility, the $or should be a single requested_by_user_id clause. Current behavior matches the spec ('leadership only sees their own POs' was interpreted as role-narrow not user-narrow).
Audit trail: every state change (submitted/approved/rejected/clarification_requested/receipt_uploaded/closed/cancelled) pushes to po.audit[] with timestamp + actor — solid.
Idempotency of scan_missing_receipts is correctly guarded by `missing_receipt_flagged: {$ne: True}` — verified empirically.
Offboarding-summary integration ships the open_pos[] + open_pos_count keys per spec. Empty in this test (no PO linked to a real employee.id), but the surface is wired.

rca of the issue: Symptom: ~half the Phase D backend tests failed with HTTP 500 on POST /api/po-requests, deserializing as JSONDecodeError. Investigation: tailed /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log → pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError: E11000 duplicate key error collection: test_database.po_requests index: po_number_1 dup key: { po_number: null }. Root cause: ensure_po_requests_indexes() used `create_index('po_number', unique=True, sparse=True)`, but MongoDB sparse indexes only skip documents MISSING the field — documents with `po_number: null` are still indexed and conflict. Since the schema legitimately writes po_number=null between submission and approval, the second concurrent or sequential null write blew up. Mitigation: dropped po_number_1 and recreated with partialFilterExpression={'po_number': {'$type': 'string'}}, which excludes both missing AND null values from the uniqueness constraint, only enforcing it on real string PO numbers. All 18 tests pass after the repair. Permanent fix requires a one-line code change in /app/backend/routes/po_requests.py (action_items #1).
